title: Hyderabad Named a Road After Trump. His Party's Rivals Did It. His Party Is Furious.
excerpt: The Congress-ruled state of Telangana unveiled 'Donald Trump Avenue' near the US Consulate. The BJP called it hypocrisy, the Left called it outrageous, and Trump called it historic.
body:
A road adjoining the US Consulate in Hyderabad now bears the name "Donald Trump Avenue." The unveiling, at a gala reception marking America's 250th anniversary, triggered a political firestorm that says more about India's domestic fault lines than it does about US-India diplomacy.

US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka jointly unveiled the plaque on Tuesday, with Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy and US Consul General Laura Williams also in attendance. The road runs through the heart of Hyderabad's tech corridor, flanked by the offices of Microsoft, Google, and Amazon — a strip of asphalt that generates more American corporate revenue than most American cities.

## Trump Notices

By Friday, Trump weighed in on Truth Social: "The new Donald Trump Avenue in Hyderabad, India — The first U.S. President to ever be honored in this way. Thank you!"

The claim to be the first is debatable — Franklin D. Roosevelt and John F. Kennedy both have streets named after them abroad — but the gesture clearly landed where it was aimed.

## The Political Knife Fight



> **"Congress has spent months accusing Modi of being "compromised" by Trump on tariffs, on US attacks on Indian-crewed tankers during the Iran war, and on immigration policy."**


What makes the story distinctly Indian is who did the naming and who is furious about it. The Telangana state government is run by the Congress party, the main opposition to Prime Minister Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party at the national level. Congress has spent months accusing Modi of being "compromised" by Trump on tariffs, on US attacks on Indian-crewed tankers during the Iran war, and on immigration policy.

The BJP pounced. "Rahul Gandhi says President Trump is hurting Indian interests," BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla wrote on X. "Then why is his government in Telangana giving the ultimate tribute to him by renaming a road after him?"

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) called the renaming "outrageous" and demanded its withdrawal, calling Trump a "war monger." Protests were organized near the site.

Congress, for its part, framed the move as pragmatic diplomacy — Hyderabad positioning itself as a gateway for American investment, regardless of who sits in the White House.

## Hyderabad's Larger Play

The Trump Avenue renaming is part of a broader initiative by the Revanth Reddy government to name prominent roads after globally recognised figures and institutions. An upcoming greenfield radial road will be named after the late industrialist Ratan Tata. A road near Google's upcoming campus — set to be the company's largest outside the United States — will be christened "Google Street."

Ambassador Gor used the occasion to underline the commercial substance beneath the ceremony. "Nowhere is the high-speed trajectory of our partnership more evident than in Hyderabad," he said. "From HITEC City to aerospace and defence, this region represents progress that is defining our bilateral momentum."

He added: "With our interim trade agreement and Mission India on track to bring over $20 billion of new investment to the United States, we are proving that America First does not mean America alone."

## Why It Matters Beyond the Name

The naming arrives at a tense moment in US-India relations. Washington has imposed steep tariffs on Indian goods. Trade negotiations are ongoing but unfinished. The recent Iran war strained the relationship further, with US forces attacking merchant vessels crewed by Indians transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

Yet both governments have continued pushing toward a trade deal that Goyal says is "very close," and Trump and Modi met at the G7 summit in France just last week. The road naming, for all its domestic drama, is a reminder that India's relationship with America plays out simultaneously at the geopolitical level and the hyperlocal one — in the UN Security Council and on a stretch of tarmac near the US Consulate.

For the diaspora, the Hyderabad tech corridor is personal. It is where many Indian Americans trace their professional roots, where parents and siblings still work, and where return trips begin. A road named after the American president, steps from where Satya Nadella once worked before becoming Microsoft's CEO, is the kind of symbolic gesture that travels. Whether it ages well depends entirely on what happens next in the relationship it claims to honour.

*Sources: Reuters, The Indian Eye, Mint, AInvest*
